entities.summary:
The Battle of Plassey was a pivotal event in world history, where on 23 June 1757, the British East India Company's forces, led by Robert Clive, decisively defeated the ruler of the Bengal region, Siraj-ud-Daula, marking the beginning of the British Raj in India.

This battle was a culmination of the British East India Company's growing influence in India, dating back to the 17th century, when they established their first trading post in 1612. The Company's expansion was fueled by their desire to monopolize the Indian spice trade and their strategic alliances with local rulers. In 1756, the Company's forces had already secured Calcutta, and Siraj-ud-Daula's forces had been weakened by internal conflicts.

The Battle of Plassey was a turning point in Indian history, as it led to the establishment of British rule, which would last for nearly two centuries. The British East India Company's influence expanded rapidly, and they began to consolidate their power, leading to the eventual collapse of the Mughal Empire. The battle also marked the beginning of a new era in Indian politics, as the British introduced their own system of administration, laws, and institutions.

The legacy of the Battle of Plassey can be seen in the continued influence of British culture, language, and institutions in India, as well as the country's ongoing struggle for independence and self-determination. Today, the battle is remembered as a symbol of Indian resistance against colonial rule and a reminder of the complexities of India's long and tumultuous history.
